utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before we ask the witness to be escorted into the courtroom, I would like to briefly move into private session for two minutes only.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I also do understand that the Prosecution would like to raise a matter in relation to the revised translation of P6857 -- 6 -- yes, 685 -- 57.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And this is an intercept that was shown to Witness Kralj on 28 October 2014. The revised English translation has been uploaded into e-court under doc ID 050471631ET. The Prosecution has spoken with the Defence and they agree to the revision. We would request that the revised revision replace the one currently there e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Bibles. The Registrar is instructed to replace the existing translation for P6857 by a new translation ID 050471631ET.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Zupljanin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I apologise, Mr. Kupresanin. Before we continue, I'd like to remind you that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. Mr. Traldi, if you're ready you may continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution have 65 ter 31775.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, I want to focus now on your evidence about the relationship between the ARK and the central authorities in Pale. Now this is an extract from the minutes of the 10th Session of the Assembly of the ARK at the assembly hall of the Banja Luka cultural centre at 1000 hours on 14 December 1991, and we see this session was chaired by yourself.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could have page 5 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We read at the top of the page in English and middle of the page in the B/C/S: "The Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina supports the integration of all Serbian territories and our representatives have been legally elected: Radovan Karadzic, Nikola Koljevic, Momcilo Krajisnik, and Vojo Kupresanin." That correctly reflects the ARK Assembly's position as of December 1991; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the regions could be established in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina under the constitution. This is under article 4 of the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina. This was not my suggestion. It was a trend which was --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to stop you. I haven't asked about the constitution of Bosnia-Herzegovina. As of December 1991, the Assembly of the ARK did, in fact, support the integration of all Serbian territories and considered its representatives to include Mr. Karadzic, Mr. Koljevic, Mr. Krajisnik, and yourself; correct?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: How do you explain that appears in the minutes of this session that you presided over?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We supported the process, and it was not up to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm not sure I understand your answer. As of -- as of the 14th of December, 1991, it's clear that the ARK Assembly supported the integration of Serb territories, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you also deny that, despite it being reflected in the minutes, the ARK Assembly considers its legal representatives to include Karadzic, Koljevic and Krajisnik?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not correct. They were not legally elected representatives of the Assembly of Krajina or the region of Krajina in any way when it came to ARK Krajina. What did Karadzic have to do with the rest of us?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, we'll look at that in a second.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: For the moment, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number 31775 receives exhibit number P7007, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Mr. Traldi, could the witness explain why the literal reading of these minutes, why they do not reflect what the position was? Because Mr. Traldi just read out what is written here.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just said what I thought about that. He put a specific question, I provided a specific question [as interpreted]. At least I think I did. It's his problem if he is not happy with the answer. I -- in this document, I don't find any other answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Traldi read to you what the minutes say and then asked you whether it's correct or not. Your answer is it's not correct. Then my question is --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then my question is why do then the minutes reflect a position you say is not correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says "excerpt."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have a document in front of me --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It says an excerpt from the minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, it's an excerpt, yes. You say it's -- the excerpt is wrong.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't tell that this is -- these are original minutes. There's no signature. There's no stamp. What is this? Documents without any paper trail?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm listening.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you are saying this excerpt, where apparently have you some doubts where it comes, this excerpt does in the reflect the position of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Krajina. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have doubts about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then one follow-up question. These excerpt -- this excerpt says that Radovan Karadzic, Nikola Koljevic, Momcilo Krajisnik, and Vojo Kupresanin are legally elected. Were you, the four of you, legally elected and elected to what exactly?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was legally elected as a deputy in the parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I was legally elected as a member in the Assembly of Republika Srpska. I was legally elected as the president of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region. All those things were legal. At that time Radovan Karadzic was the president of Serbian Democratic Party, legally elected. Radovan Karadzic and the others did not instruct us to make decisions at the Assembly of the Autonomous Region. We were not duty-bound by their positions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P2720.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a intercepted conversation between yourself and General Kukanjac, then the head of the 2nd Military District, in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 2 in the English and the top of page 3 in the B/C/S, we read in the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say: "Well, we must and now we are waiting for Karadzic to return from Europe and tell us what we are to do next. I personally think, General, that I won't do anything until he returns, when he comes whatever he tells us we will do. He is now for us the Supreme Commander and we have no other commander. The Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, on the one side, and the Serb people in the situation they are in, on the other. We have our commander, it is that man, we must obey him, you understand us, we understand you." Now, that man you are saying is your commander who you must obey is President Karadzic; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask my colleague to give the time-frame of this document to the witness so he understands about which time --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, but it depends which month, heavily. For --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I said the month of April, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay, sorry. I didn't hear it. Sorry. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's accepted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'll repeat my question, sir. The man you are saying is your Supreme Commander who you must obey is President Radovan Karadzic; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was not the Supreme Commander. I may have put it that way. He was only the president of the party, so he was not in a position to be the Supreme Commander. However, we in the Serbian people who found ourselves in such a position when the Yugoslav People's Army was leaving --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, let me stop you there. When you are referring to the Supreme Commander, were you referring to Radovan Karadzic? That's the question. Or did you have anyone else on your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was head. He was not supreme commander. He was head. That's how I would describe him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I didn't ask you to describe his position. I did ask you whether in this portion of this intercepted conversation, whether you referred to Mr. Karadzic, did you or did you not? Whatever his position was.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I meant him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say in paragraph 34 of your statement, sir, that this intercept shows you did not have contact with Karadzic and Pale. I'd put to you that, in fact, what it shows is you're simply saying that he's in Europe and you're just waiting for him to come back and give you your marching orders; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really can't remember where he was. Maybe he was in Europe. He was probably there. I don't know how I found out where he was. It was only logical for us to expect him to voice his opinion, his position, because that's what Kukanjac had asked from us. I don't know what else I could tell you. Why I would have I know where the president of the party was at the time. I don't know where he was. Should I have known?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't ask you where he was at the time. What I put to you, and I'll do it very clearly, is that your description of this intercept in your statement is incorrect and what you are actually saying is when he comes back, he will give you your marching orders and you must obey them. That's what we see you saying; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He never issued any orders to us. Nor were we duty-bound to carry out his orders. What I said, I said it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, are you not answering the questions, unfortunately. You again and again give your comments on what was said, whereas what you are asked is to confirm what you said and what that actually means; that is, wait until he's back and then we'll receive his orders. Is that the gist of what you said here, or is there anything else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Very well. Let it be that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm done with this document now, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And it is -- I just have to check.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's in evidence already. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, sir, one leader in the ARK who had close relations with Pale was Mr. Brdjanin, the Crisis Staff president; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that he had close relations with Pale. Actually, he was more in conflict with Pale than in close relations. That's my personal opinion. Yes, yes, exactly. He very often clashed with Pale.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, could we have 65 ter 31770.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's your OTP interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm looking for page 68 in the English and the bottom of page 100 in the B/C/S. I think we still have page 1 in the English. And we're looking for page 68.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So you're asked here: "Are you aware of Radoslav Brdjanin visiting areas outside Banja Luka during 1992?" You say: "No." And you're asked: "He did not visit or are you not aware of his visits?" And you respond: "I don't know anything, whether he went or didn't go. We didn't socialise."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we'll turn to the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "He had his own world. His people were the top, on the top." When you said that, you were referring to the people at the top of the structures of political authority in the Republika Srpska; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was that. I don't know that he was very close with the top of the tops at Pale. But Brdjanin was specific in the sense that whenever he had an occasion to talk to the top echelons, he did and that concerned co-operation between Pale and Banja Luka. As a matter of fact, you're saying that he was a yes man or that his only agenda was to forward his career. Yes, you may say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So can I take it you confirm what you said in this portion of your OTP interview?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm also aware of the other side and that was that he very often clashed with Pale. I -- you had an intercept of a conversation between Brdjanin, Karadzic, and myself, and Karadzic -- Brdjanin's name is always mentioned as somebody who was disruptive.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's look at one example of an intercept between Karadzic and Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have P2636. 2636.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm looking for page 2 in both languages. This is an intercepted conversation between them in July 1991. And we can see in both languages an underlined sentence that says: "We have done the one today." Looking just below that, we see Mr. Karadzic says: "Nothing nothing have done, if you have brought decision on referendum, it would have been terrible." And Mr. Brdjanin responses: "We have not, have not, we obeyed." What we see here is he is confirming that he obeyed an order he'd received from Mr. Karadzic and the authorities in Pale; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please don't put me in situations where I can say only yes or no. Could I be allowed to say something more about this referendum, just a few sentences? I need to explain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First I'd ask that you answer my question, sir. What we see here is Mr. Brdjanin confirming that he obeyed an order he received from Mr. Karadzic and the authorities in Pale; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, did he not obey it. That's why Radovan called him and only then did he obey. So he did not obey. He caused confusion and then he obeyed and made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 08469. And that's been marked for identification as P6997, pending a selection of material. And I'm looking for page 53 in the English and middle of page 46 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, this is the session of the SDS on the 12th of July, 1991 at which you were elected to the Main Board. And here we see a portion of Mr. Brdjanin's remarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we're waiting for the B/C/S page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see below the note of applause, that he says: "I personally think that regions strengthen the government in Sarajevo. If anyone thinks different, they who interpret it differently surely are trying to con our greatest leadership." "I am a man who abides by two principles: I obey and respect those who are above me, all those who are under my command must obey me." So what we see here, again, is Mr. Brdjanin confirming that he believes he has the obligation to obey and respect those above him, the leadership of the SDS; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It turns how that was his rule. Those were above him, he obeyed them, and he demanded to be obeyed from those below him. That was his life philosophy. That's how things were.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Separate from his relationship with the ARK, President Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I'm done with this document, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- also had control through the political chain of command of the presidents of municipal governments; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Political control? Probably he did have an impact on the conduct and all the political relations in the Serbian Democratic Party in municipalities. It was only logical that it followed the work of the Serbian Democratic Party in municipalities. Municipalities as municipalities were in certain a way states in a state. I was the president of Krajina, and I did not have any control over any municipality. The statute of the region did not present any particular positions with regard to the presidents of the municipalities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you've again gone beyond the question I asked to your relationship with municipalities. What I'm asking you to confirm, and I believe you had, is President Karadzic having control of the presidents of municipal governments. And we'll get to the relationship between the ARK and the municipalities in a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, Mr. Traldi, you mean political control.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Political control, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So I do want to look at one policy example.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31771.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This will be a transcript of an intercepted conversations between Radovan Karadzic and Radislav Vukic dated the 27th of September, 1991. As it comes up, in paragraph 22 of your statement you suggest that in November 1991 you insisted in the ARK Assembly that representatives of the SDA, HDZ, and SDP who were in managerial positions should be replaced and Dr. Karadzic opposed that. Now Mr. Vukic, who he's speaking with here, is one of the other political leaders in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was no political leader of the ARK. He was simply a municipal president of the SDS in Banja Luka. Deputies in the assembly wielded more influence than Vukic. He could not influence our work. And when I say that, I mean the decisions of the district assembly or similar things. Vukic could not exert any influence over our work. I don't know whether he tried, but he certainly did not have any influence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, turning to page 2 in the English and the bottom of page 2 in the B/C/S, Dr. Karadzic asks: "In whose hands is Radio Banja Luka?" And Vukic responds: "I beg your pardon?" Karadzic asks again: "In whose hands is Radio Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to the next page in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Vukic responds: "A Muslim is a director." Karadzic responds: "What the fuck?" And Vukic says: "Shall I replace him straight away, let him go to fucking hell? And Karadzic says: "Come on, replace him immediately. Appoint a man of yours. These are war times. Appoint -- if he is not listening to you, appoint a man of yours." So what we see here is that Dr. Karadzic's position, in fact, was that the Muslim director of Radio Banja Luka should be replaced immediately; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, a Muslim was not a director of Radio Banja Luka. It was Mrs. Bozic. However, the IT centre head of Banja Luka RTV was Mr. Smajic. Now, what his exact position in the IT centre in Banja Luka is something I don't remember. I do remember him well. He was not removed until Rajko Vasic came along who was the head of the radio and television company. So it wasn't a Muslim who was the director of Radio Banja Luka. It was Mrs. Bozic. It was a mistake. I may have had Smajic in mind at the IT centre. As for this conversation, I don't know. Well, he did ask for assistance and Radovan supported him. That is obvious. Although we, in the Krajina, did not think along those lines. I know about Smajic no one removed him and he simply left Banja Luka perhaps a year after these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd tender 65 ter 31771.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31771 receives exhibit number P7008, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence. Witness, by giving your own recollection of the events, you are moving away from what you were asked. You were asked whether Karadzic here - and that seems to be the language he uses - whether Karadzic was instructing or ordering to replace a person whose name is not even mentioned but who was a Muslim and to be replaced immediately. Now whether that happened and who it was is a different matter, but you again and again are moving away from what Mr. Traldi is asking you. Mr. Traldi is asking you whether hearing this, seeing this, whether this is what it looks like, that it's such an instruction was given. Whether it was followed up is a different matter. Who it was is also another question. But the question by Mr. Traldi simply was: Is Mr. Karadzic here giving a clear instruction that a Muslim, he was told was the director, should be replaced.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. A simple yes in the beginning would have saved a lot of time. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If I may just say something. According to this intercept here, sir, Ms. Bozic who you say was -- in whose hands you say the radio was, is mentioned just below there as the main editor, not the person in whose hands the TV station was. Do you have any comment on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, I'm not sure what she was. I just know that she was the main person on the radio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So what you said earlier, you are not sure of. You are just guessing when you said she was the person in whose hands the radio was? Her position is being explained here in this intercept. She is the main editor. I see you pull your lips. You're not answering -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31768.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, sir, a moment ago you said we in the Krajina did not think along those lines. In fact, the ARK authorities, including the Crisis Staff, issued decisions on the dismissal of non-Serbs from a number of positions in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The 65 ter you called has not been recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, 31768 and I see we do have it on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So, sir, before we get to the document, I'll repeat my question. The ARK authorities, including the ARK Crisis Staff, issued decisions on the dismissal of non-Serbs from a number of positions in 1992; right.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please do not make this link between us and the Crisis Staff. We did not establish it. The ARK Crisis Staff was probably an operations body of the government of RS. We did not create it. We did not influence its conclusions or their implementation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff of the ARK did not have --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You were a member of that Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, yes or no, it did issue decisions on the removal of non-Serbs from particular positions in 1992.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was one of the conclusions of the Crisis Staff, to have people in key positions in publicly owned enterprises who were not members of the SDS - I'll say it again, who were not members of the SDS - should be replaced by members of the SDS. It was a rule across all of Bosnia-Herzegovina in the political arena. The SDS removed all public enterprise directors who were not members of the SDS. It was a rule, and it was accepted. Now why would that be a sin? Even before that, people were being removed, before this decision of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you -- sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff could not --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you recall who made that rule?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who made that rule? Well, there were elections before that. At the time there was still the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. After the elections we gained power.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: And it a rule that the party in power has influence over key positions and it is also regulated by law.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's look at this document. This is a decision by the Serb municipality of Doboj. It's being sent to the Ministry of Justice of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina. And it's dated the 24th June 1992. Directing your attention to the bottom of the page, we can see that it reflects a proposal by yourself as president of the ARK, and is -- is also signed by Municipal President, Drago Ljubican. What we see in this document is a proposal that three men be replaced as public prosecutors in Doboj and three other men be appointed. And at point 4 we read: "Also, pursuant to Articles 1 and 2 of the decision by the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, which stipulate that every high-level post within state institutions may be filled solely by staff of Serbian ethnicity alone ..." And then it shows who is being proposed to be removed. So this is an implementation of the ARK Crisis Staff decision on dismissing non-Serbs from high positions; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the three names of the men to be dismissed: Midhat Demirovic, son of Abdurahman; and Senad Serement, son of Ibrahim. Those are Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But how come my signature is on this document when the ARK Assembly never engaged in removing or appointing any personnel? How could I have ordered this when it was within the remit of the Crisis Staff? What would the Autonomous District have to do with this? I never issued such decisions and I did not influence any personnel issues. I did not even appoint any directors, let alone judges or prosecutors. How come my name appears on this document? It is unclear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I -- sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Crisis Staff did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And I just have one more question on the document. Anto Pekez, son of Stipo, that's a Croat name; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender 65 ter 31768.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we decide on that. Witness, do you say this is not my signature or it -- it's not fully understood why it is there? What's your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am trying to say that the removal of personnel in the judiciary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, Witness, Witness, would you please answer my question. My question is not whether it was your competence or not. That may be a follow-up question. My question is where you say what does my signature do on this document, are you saying it's not your signature or do you say, Well, there must be -- I still do not understand why it is there. Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm trying to say that this is a precedent of sorts. I've never engaged in such matters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But the question was not whether you engaged in such matters before but whether you recognise this to be your signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then you have explained that it's odd that it is there, but at the same time you acknowledge for a fact that it is your signature.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never dealt with this. That is why I am doubtful about it all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I maintain my request to tender the document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document number 31768 receives exhibit number P7009, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P7009 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, the Chamber has received evidence that the decision on dismissals was also implemented in Prijedor municipality. That's true, isn't it? The municipalities would implement decisions by the ARK Crisis Staff, such as this decision on dismissing non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, Prijedor municipality was not in the district. As of the municipalities -- in terms of municipalities who joined the district, Prijedor was not one of them. So the Crisis Staff could not can exert any influence over personnel policy in the municipality of Prijedor, I wonder.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, let's look at the documents, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit P6948.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At page 1 here, we see here the ARK Crisis Staff decision that was referred to in the Doboj document we just saw. We see it's dated the 22nd of June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 2, in both languages -- sorry, 3 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see a version of this document bearing the handwritten note for immediate delivery to the president of the municipality Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now turning to page 3 in the English and I believe it's page 5 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see a signed, stamped document emanating from the Crisis Staff of Prijedor municipality deciding that it should forward the decision of the Crisis Staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina for implementation. So, in fact, the Prijedor Crisis Staff implemented this decision; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. No decision of the Autonomous Region Crisis Staff was binding on any municipality. It was only a suggestions. Had it been binding, it would have carried sanctions with it. Not one were binding. They were suggestions. Had Prijedor refused to implement this instruction by the Crisis Staff, nothing would have happened. That is why I think you're wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, first I'd put to you --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could go back to page 1, both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to put to you two points about this. First, it's called a decision, not a suggestion; correct? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, perhaps it was a conclusion of the Crisis Staff. I don't know whether it was a proposal or a decision. Crisis Staff had conclusions and they wanted them implemented. This may have been accompanied by a conclusion. Now as for Prijedor, I doubt they implemented it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, you said it was just a suggestion. Mr. Traldi asks you whether this document says it's a suggestion or a decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I haven't read the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you only need to read one word, top centre of the page. Can you read out that word for us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, the witness is allowed to read --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read it. I read it. It says decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Traldi, if the witness wants to read it, it may be denied half way that it's not really a decision. Or whatever comes, he's entitled to do that and you should not tell him that he only should look at one word. Whether it finally would support any other conclusion is a different matter, but if the witness says I haven't read it, then you should not instruct him just to read one word where you put the whole of the document to him. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, discussing the whole of document, do you agree with me that point 4 also refers to this as a decision which shall enter into force?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A Crisis Staff decision cannot be binding on anyone or be into force. How could it be when the Crisis Staff has no power of sanction? It was an operations RS government organ for crisis situations. This was a crisis situation. However, it was not binding on the leadership of Prijedor municipality to implement it. The Crisis Staff could not do that. So it was a non-binding decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I take it we all agree this is referred to as a decision that shall enter into force.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31770, page 33 in the English and 46 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This will be another part of your OTP interview. You were asked here did Brdjanin give orders to presidents of municipalities about what he wanted carried out, and you responded: "Well, you see, I asked myself that question. Certain things happened in Krajina. I'm interested to what extent was the ARK Crisis Staff connected to the peripheral." You were asked if you mean municipal Crisis Staffs, and you say: "Yes, yes. That is a great mystery for me." How is it that when, in 2001, when your recollection was fresher, as you testified on Thursday, you claimed it was a mystery to you to what extent the ARK Crisis Staff was connected to the municipal Crisis Staffs, and today you claim that you are quite sure of its relationship with the municipal Crisis Staffs and you are minimizing that relationship?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not minimizing anything. I know what the Crisis Staff was and what its role was. I know what their possibilities were. I know to what extent their proposals could be implemented. Their powers were limited under the law. There's something that confuses me in what you said. We did have an ARK Crisis Staff but not a Banja Luka Crisis Staff, so it is my impression that the Banja Luka Crisis Staff moved up to the level of ARK Crisis Staff. First of all, no one from the Krajina sitting on that staff was from the Krajina itself. Everyone was from Banja Luka only. Nobody from Drvar, Petrovac, or Srbac. Everyone in the ARK Crisis Staff was from Banja Luka. They were residents of Banja Luka. It is my impression that sometimes the roles were reversed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, where were you from?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do hail from Srbac by I worked in Banja Luka; hence, I did not represent Srbac municipality. It had its own representative and he was perhaps the only one who came from time to time. The rest did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In fact --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness repeat his last sentence. It was inaudible.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're being asked to repeat your last sentence, sir.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the ARK Crisis Staff were not people from the region. They were all from Banja Luka. The Banja Luka Crisis Staff was never set up, and I wonder why it was not when the government instructed that Crisis Staff municipal staffs be established. They did not say that a regional Crisis Staff had to be established.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the Banja Luka Crisis Staff took over the role for the entire region.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: A very specific question: Who was the Srbac representative you had in mind a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milos Milincic, president of the municipality. He was a guest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, he testified here a month ago and he testified that presidents of the various municipalities were by their function members of the ARK Crisis Staff. That's, in fact, the truth; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Their first and last names of the people who comprised the ARK Crisis Staff. There were between 10 and 15. It is clear who was there but nobody was from the district. Everyone was from Banja Luka. The roles were turned. Who ordered the establishment of the ARK Crisis Staff, I have never received such a document from the government.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, again you've gone well beyond my question. Milorad Sajic similarly testified last week that every Monday the presidents of and representatives from various ARK municipalities would come to Banja Luka every Monday and meet with the ARK Crisis Staff. You're aware of that too; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I occasionally attended the sessions of the Crisis Staff and I basically never saw some people from the Autonomous Region. I don't remember seeing anyone. The 10 or 15 people were members of the Crisis Staff of the region, including General Talic, but I never saw anyone from Drvar or Celinac, from any municipality of the regions at the sessions of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every municipality --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Brdjanin was from Celinac; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Brdjanin was in Banja Luka working for the Ministry of Urban Planning. Had nothing to do with Celinac. They had their own president of the municipality who came, Sveto Kovacevic. They had their own Crisis Staff. Every municipality did. But Banja Luka did not have one. Hence, it is confusing. How come there were people from Banja Luka in the ARK Crisis Staff, whereas where there was no Banja Luka Crisis Staff, and yet the government ordered the establishment of a Crisis Staff in the municipality. So people from the city were in the ARK staff. It was confusing for me then when I provided the statement and it is still confusing. There were things happening that were done in an underhanded way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I see we're almost at the time for the break. Before we get there, I'd put to you that based on your own evidence you simply do not know the extent of the relationship between the ARK Crisis Staff and the municipal Crisis Staffs. That's what's come out from your various answers; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you that the decisions of the ARK Crisis Staff were not binding on the municipalities in the periphery or in the region because there were no sanctions. They could and they didn't need to. Some did, some did not. So they were not binding. That is my response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Before we take that break. Witness, you said, and -- let me find it. Yes. When asked about Mr. Brdjanin you said he was working in Banja Luka, he had got nothing to with Celinac. They had their own president of the municipality who came. He came where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He could come if there was need. But he had his own Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, you're changing from one line to another. You said he came, not he could come. But you said he came. Came where? Is that the meeting of the -- is that the meeting of the ARK Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. He could have come. But as I said, I never saw any municipal president at the Crisis Staff. I never saw any of them there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You say he could come, you said he came, and you say I never saw him there. Okay. That's -- we have to evaluate that evidence and all the other evidence we received on this matter. Mr. Traldi, any further questions before the break or not --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Not before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then we'll take the break. Mr. Kupresanin, we take a break of 20 minutes. We'd like to see you back after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. President, two brief matters before the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: First, I'd seek to add this page to P6994, MFI, once portions are selected to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And second, just to correct myself a moment ago, I believe I said I said Mr. Sajic testified last week. I believe it's now the week before last.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We are in a new week now, yes, Mr. Traldi. We take a break and we resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, waiting for the witness to come in. I'm addressing parties now about the scheduling of early next year. Mr. Lukic, we received a message that you would have one witness available for the week where you more or less you requested not to sit. Of course we do not know whether it's the -- whether there are any chance that others would come as well. We also have -- are considering whether you would prefer, if there would be only one witness, and we're still in a -- the phase of considering matters, whether it would help you out if we would sit five days the week after that but then not to sit that one week and use the fifth day, if you would be able to conclude the evidence of that witness during one day, and if that would also be a possibility for the Prosecution then to give you an option. But, again, we -- of course, we first like to have more witnesses. But if it was just that one witness, whether it would be an option to -- to hear the evidence of that witness in one day and then to skip that week.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was more hopeful before, Your Honours, when I told you that we are still trying to get more witnesses for that week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But I think where we stand now is that we can have only have that one, and we -- if Your Honours decide that way, we would accept your proposition to sit five days the next week. It would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, at least --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- preferable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- we are --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I didn't even think about it but it would be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- excellent --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are considering it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- [overlapping speakers].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, of course, one of the issues would be whether it would fit into one day and that depends also on the time for cross-examination needed. I just raised it with you so that you can think about and we'd like to hear any further responses later today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Kupresanin, we'll now continue the -- to hear your evidence in cross-examination. May I draw your attention to one thing which seems to brother you and may brother others as well. It is that you are often telling us whether things could have happened or whether they should have happened, whereas it seems that Mr. Traldi is mainly focusing on one what he, at least on the basis of documentation, thinks -- thinks has happened. Now, there is a clear distinction between what happens. Sometimes even things are happening that could not happen if everything would be in accordance with all the rules and -- and there's another option that perhaps that things should not have happened. But Mr. Traldi, again and again, is asking you on what he thinks happened, looking at the documents, such as that there was a decision, because he reads there is a decision, whereas you're explaining that there could not be a decision or at least there should not have been a decision. Let's try to distinguish those very clearly and first answer his questions about what he sees in the documents that has happened. Could you clearly make that distinction in trying to first focus your answer on what is asked. Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm go doing ask you a few question you now about Mr. Brdjanin. Now other people told you that they had heard Mr. Brdjanin say on television that only a thousand Muslims could stay in Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I heard. What I heard on TV was that --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- the B and H television one day asked him about what happened in Banja Luka --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Finish your sentence.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Journalists in Banja Luka asked him how desirable it would be if the Muslims came back, and then he said one -- he gave a percentage. I don't remember the percentage. What I know about his statement has to do with the potential number of people who should return to Banja Luka, but what I say and what others say about what he said does not necessarily have to be true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, your question was unclear. You said other people told you that -- let me see. It's ... other people told Mr. Kupresanin, yes, then I withdraw my observation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We still have your OTP interview up.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have page 43 in the English and page 64 in the B/C/S. And towards the bottom of this page in English towards the top of the page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You were asked: "Have you heard him on TV saying that only a thousand Muslims would stay in Banja Luka? " You said: "I didn't hear that myself, but I heard that he had said that." You were asked: "Who told you that? Other Muslims or Serbs or everybody was saying it? " And you responded: "Serbs told me that, but a normal person cannot say such a thing." And then in the same paragraph, you mentioned Hitler. So does that refresh your recollection as to whether you were told during the war that Brdjanin had gone on television and said only a thousand Muslims could stay in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember that. People said all kinds of things. I cannot remember that specific case or the number 1.000. I don't know who said that or where this number of 1.000 came from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Do you remember hearing from many Muslims that they were afraid of him?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it was not pleasant to listen to that kind of talk. Of course it was not pleasant.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Specifically, do you remember hearing from Muslims that they were afraid of Mr. Brdjanin, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard that -- that they were afraid or that they were being frightened. I don't know if that's the same thing, but I heard that they were afraid.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Of Mr. Brdjanin, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the things he said, in his addresses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you considered as of 2001 that Brdjanin wanted to impose radical nationalist solutions for the benefit of one national group against the rights of other national groups; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In my opinion, first of all, Brdjanin in my opinion was not an extremist nationalist. As for him being a nationalist or not, that's another story all together. But I don't consider that he was a nationalist. What was Brdjanin, in fact, like?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He found himself in that position at that particular moment --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have page 56 of the same interview in the English, page 82 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what I'm going to do for the remainder of this portion of the examination, sir, is simply read to you portions of the interview you gave 13 years ago that you testified was truthful and was given when your recollection was fresher. You were asked here whether Brdjanin was one of the most radical in the Krajina, and you asked what radical means.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so beginning at line 31 in the English and 16 in the B/C/S, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You're told: "A very fair comment. When I say 'radical,' I mean radical nationalists, someone who wants to impose solutions, radical nationalist solutions for the benefit of one national group against the rights of other national groups." You replied: "I understood. Well, judging by his appearances or, and his attitude, what he said, Brdjanin had all those elements and more than that." You were asked: "What do you mean by more than that?" And you responded: "Well, this 10 per cent thing. Or what Tudjman said, a third of Serbs will be killed ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I think we're turning to the next page, I apologise, in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: "Or what Tudjman said, a third of Serbs will be killed, a third of Serbs will be converted, and a third of Serbs will be forced out or deported and he did that." You were asked: "When you say the 10 per cent thing, you mean the statements Brdjanin made that only a few per cent of Muslims and Croats can remain in the Krajina?" And you answered: "Yes, that's what I heard from you, but also I heard it from the Serbs." So that's the truth, what you said in your interview in 2001, that Brdjanin had all the elements of a radical nationalist and more and that you'd heard that, as you testified a moment ago, that only a few per cent of Muslims and Croats could remain in the Krajina, in his position; right.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was his position, that 1 per cent or certain number of people should come back. It was expressed in terms of percentages, but I don't remember what that figure, the percentage, actually was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And do you stand by the truthfulness and accuracy of the portion of your interview that I read to you a moment ago?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Given the qualification, I'll seek to that add to P6994 Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But for the most part. In what part do you not agree, from what was read to you as your previous statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The way it's formulated. Brdjanin as a nationalist and an extreme nationalist, all these are terms for analysis. His statements do lead to that sort of conclusion, but he was not like that as a person. I did give a statement about it, and I do stand by the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. That was -- you earlier made that reservation but apparently I now understand that you stand by the interview you gave which was just read to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we page 68 in the English and 100 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you were asked --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Beginning at the top of the page in the English, and actually if we could go back to the bottom of page 99 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You were asked: "Do you think Radoslav Brdjanin is a war criminal?" And you respond: "I think that Radoslav Brdjanin ask responsible for certain things." You were asked: "What are those things ...?" And you say: "And for those things he should be prosecuted." You're asked: "What are those things he is responsible for?" And you say: "I cannot qualify him or I cannot say that he's a war criminal. There's an institution for that. When such an institution qualifies him or decides that he's a war criminal, then I will do it as well. What I put on his soul are statements in, to which other national ... people of other nationality, nationalities had great problems and probably those statements made them move, partly." You were asked: "The statements that he was making on television and in the media, in your opinion, was there a cause to insight Serbs living in the ARK region to fight or to start a conflict with Muslims and Croats and to commit the crimes that were committed in the ARK region? " You say: "I don't think that he had any influence before the war. What I think was bad was during the war, what happened during the war." And you were asked: "So, during the war, did he incite the local Serbian population in the Krajina to commit the crimes against Muslims and Croats?" You responded: "I think that his statements contributed to the great danger that, that Croats and Muslims were put into and probably one part of them moved out because of those things." Do you stand by the truthfulness and accuracy of the portion of your OTP interview in 2001 that I've just read out to you?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm trying to remember now what I said approximately 14 years ago. And I can say at the end, if it's the end, regarding Brdjanin, that his statements were what they were and that they created fear among the people. As for how much those statements contributed to people leaving the area, it probably did have an effect to a certain degree. So my statement there is more or less that. Brdjanin did not cause the war. Politics caused the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the war started, all the parties --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Again, I haven't asked you about the causes of the war, and I appreciate that your explaining the same points you explained in that part of your interview. But can I ask you to simply answer, yes or no, whether you stand by the truthfulness and accuracy of the portion of your prior interview that I read out to you.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: All right. Very well. I do stand by it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you believed that Mr. Brdjanin was serving a purpose to someone through expressing these extreme views; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say whether he was representatives of somebody's politics or not, whether he was doing something out of his own head, or based on somebody else's ideas. I think that he did not do these things based on what was going on in his mind at the time. That would be my assessment. I don't know what I can say about it, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have page 68 in the English and the bottom of page 100 in the B/C/S. And we looked at this portion of your interview before in a different context, and it's just below the portion we have on our screens now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You say: "I don't know anything, whether he went or he didn't go. We didn't socialise. He had his own world, his people were the top, on the top." That's the part we looked at before. And then you say: "Let me just say something, all his speeches and all those statements and actions could have been cut off by somebody and somebody could have shortened his horns. I wonder why people who were able to do that didn't do it, because such statements and such accents, actions of his, only damaged or created damage for the Serb people. So the president of the country could have done it, the president of the assembly could have, parliament, I'm sorry, the parliament, president of the parliament, president of the government or the prime minister. Why did they tolerate it, maybe they agreed with him, I don't know." First, do you stand by the truthfulness and accuracy of this portion of your interview as I've read it out to you today?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was war time, I think, and there were such statements, warmongering statements, on all sides --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and that was the reaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Again, I've asked you a very simple question: Do you stand by the truthfulness and accuracy of the portion of your interview that I just read out to you, yes or no.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you testified in the Karadzic case that you believed Mr. Brdjanin was in communication with the army about these positions of his; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You believed he had an ideal relationship with the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not with the army but with some people; specific people in the army. He socialised with them often.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Who do you have in mind?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most probably he spent time with some officers. I don't know who I can mention specifically. Perhaps some lower-ranking officers. Some officers like that. He often referred to the army and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31772, page 46.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And as it comes up, this will be a portion of your sworn testimony in the Karadzic case. Mr. Tieger asked you about the same portion of your OTP interview that I just asked you about, and you said: "I see that I've said that and I probably did, but I'll be more precise now. I believe Mr. Brdjanin was in communication with the army on this subject. That's my opinion. And I believe that he did not communicate on that subject at all with Mr. Karadzic. He adored officers and generals. I was sometimes in conflict with them but his relationship with them was ideal." Now, in the Karadzic case you did not suggest that it was lower-ranking officers that Mr. Brdjanin was in communication with about his extreme views. You said it was officers and generals; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. He mentioned the army a lot, but I don't know actually who he was in contact with, what those -- who those officers were. I mean, I would refer to them often as a factor of threat. I think he did that in order to seem or to appear more powerful in our eyes. But I don't recall the names of the officers. He did used to refer to them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I wanted to -- to be fair, I want to be quite clear what I'm putting to you now. What I'm putting to you is, in the Karadzic case you testified that it was officer and generals Mr. Brdjanin was in communication with about this. Just now, you said that you don't, in fact, know who he was in communication with about it. What I'm putting to you is when you attempted to limit it to lower-ranking officers a moment ago, you did so because you were testifying on behalf of one of the generals in that army. That's true, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that the general who is sitting here knew and he defended the Serbian people at a certain point in time. Some JNA generals escaped. If it hadn't been for him, the Serbian people would have been in big trouble. So the Serbian people do have the -- lots of reasons to be very grateful to this general who is sitting here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] We turn into closed session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Witness, Mr. Kupresanin, the Chamber would have preferred that would you have answered the question that was put to you by Mr. Traldi rather than to give the comment which was not solicited from you and which apparently has led to some reaction in this courtroom. Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd ask that the Karadzic testimony also be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 31772 receives number P7010, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And for both we'll make a proposed selection at the conclusion of the testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the Defence can make any suggestions to add for context other parts. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can we have P353, page 53 in the English and the B/C/S transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: As it comes up, sir, did you ever have occasion to meet with General Mladic during the war?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Did I have the opportunity, yes. During assembly sessions I had the opportunity. I wasn't very close to General Mladic. We even had some conflicts, disagreement regarding the conduct of the army and so on. I had the opportunity or I was an intermediary in his appointment. Radovan Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- asked me at one point to seek an officer in the JNA --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I've asked you a very simple question and again you've gone beyond it. This is a portion of General Mladic's notebook from the 2nd of June, 1992. It's a meeting with the leaderships of the Bosnian Krajina, the SRK, and unit commanders of the 1st Krajina Corps, and the commander of the air force and anti-aircraft defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now if we could turn to page 57 in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Before I get to the substance of the meeting, we see your name and that you discuss events regarding Doboj. So, in fact, you did meet with General Mladic during the war outside of assembly sessions; right? At least on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, turning to page 54 in both languages, General Mladic is recording for most of this page remarks by Mr. Brdjanin and Mr. Brdjanin says at the second bullet point: "Everything in the ARK is done at KS level." That's Crisis Staff level; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if he used the abbreviation KS, then he did. I don't know. I don't know whether Brdjanin was at that session. If you say that he was, then he was. I don't know whether you know at all why that meeting was organised. I believe I do know, so maybe you will allow me to explain. If not, I hope I've answered your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: For the moment, what I'm asking you is KS here refers to Crisis Staff; right? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Below that, Mr. Brdjanin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, do you know any other explanation for the acronym KS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, the Crisis Staff was never active on the breakthrough of the corridor. At least not officially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, Witness, that's not what I asked you. The question is whether -- we have to interpret what is written there. It says KS. You say I don't know whether it was meant to mean Crisis Staff. My question to now is: Do you know of any other explanation for an abbreviation which is KS?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have an explanation for this abbreviation KS. I don't know what this refers to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but if you don't have --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You are aware that KS is often used as an abbreviation for Crisis Staff. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I don't. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You -- you do not know that KS is the usual abbreviation for Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But a few lines ago -- let me get that on my screen again. A few moments ago, it was read to you: "Everything in the ARK is done at KS level." And Mr. Traldi then asked you: "That's Crisis Staff level; right?" You said: "Well, if he used the abbreviation KS, then he did." And then you continued saying that you do not know who was present and you do not know whether -- why it was at all organised, that meeting. You -- you apparently seem to accept that KS is the usual abbreviation for Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Line 42 -- page 42, line 1, he explicitly said: "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: "I don't know," and he continued --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He was -- he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: These are matters not to be discussed when the witness listens in. "I don't know. I don't know whether Brdjanin was at that session." So whether the --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No. If he used the abbreviation KS --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic we stop this discussion we have an opportunity to later analyse that. My simple question is you are not aware of KS being the usual abbreviation for Crisis Staff? Because this Chamber, let me be clear to you, has seen the abbreviation KS for Crisis Staff hundreds of times, and this Chamber has never heard any other explanation for that abbreviation as it referring to Crisis Staff. Therefore, I'm asking you whether you are familiar with any other understanding of what the abbreviation KS stands for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know. But the official name of the institution is Crisis Staff, not KS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, that is evading the question because abbreviations usually are not the official names. Let's leave it to that. Mr. Traldi, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: May I put one --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- additional question. Who was president of the Crisis Staff of the ARK?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. That clarifies the situation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Below the part I read to you, Mr. Brdjanin says: "It's a mistake to appoint agents from the centre." What he's saying there is that there isn't a need to -- for the republic-level authorities to appoint a commissioner in the ARK because he'll carry out their decisions, he and the Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know nothing about that. I know nothing about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to page 55, Mr. Brdjanin is still speaking, refers in the lower part of the page to the problem of the Krajina, which he says is 14.500 Muslims. This is a reference to the number of Muslims being held prisoner around the ARK at the beginning of June 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were not that many Muslim prisoners. I don't know how many times were in Prijedor. There was Omarska, there was Keraterm, those were two collection centres. I don't know how many people were held there. 14.000 is totally out of the question. He may have said that but that's not the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Where it says that those were prisoners? I cannot find.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I put to the witness that that was what he was talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's the question, Mr. Lukic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to the next page, page 56, still Mr. Brdjanin, and while we do, do you recall what in your opinion he did mean by 14.500 Muslims? There are clearly more than 14.500 Muslims among the pre-war population of the ARK.

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why he would use that figure, I don't know. I don't know why he said that at all. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, as far as the transcript is concerned, looking at page 45, line 13, it's my recollection that the witness was translated and was interpreted as having said that's not the truth. Is that everyone's recollection, then?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mine too, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm trying to find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It reads: "He may have said that...," it's about the number. I think I heard --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's not the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- that's not the truth. That's what we heard. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now on this page at the end of his remarks, Mr. Brdjanin says: "About prisoners and refugees? A position, please, at the highest level." Here he is asking for guidance from the republic-level authorities what to do about prisoners and refugees in the ARK; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to some of those prisoners. I'll start with Omarska camp. First, I'm going to ask to you confirm that you went to Omarska at President Karadzic's direction; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you were at Omarska camp, you saw several hundred or maybe a thousand people sitting in an asphalt area between two buildings; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You went to the director's office and asked if there were any deputies from the assembly there as prisoners?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now the director was Mr. Mejakic and he was wearing a blue police uniform; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a number of police uniforms there. I don't remember who the director was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you took a detainee named Mevludin Sejmenovic out of the camp; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And in his presence, you called President Karadzic to report to President Karadzic about how your visit had gone; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mevludin Sejmenovic, myself, and Mr. Karadzic found ourselves at the assembly building in Banja Luka and we discussed many things. And we also were in communication with President Karadzic. It is true that we were in communication with him, it is true that we had a meeting, and it's true that we talked. All that is true. All that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Specifically in his presence you made a phone call -- shortly after taking him, you made a phone call to President Karadzic to report to him on what had happened; right?

utterances.speaker: VOJO KUPRESANIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now you said in your interview in 2001 that you were angry about what you saw in Omarska because you thought it would hurt the Serb cause.
